title: Types of Discontinuity: Jump
notes: **Definition.** f has a jump discontinuity at a when LHL and RHL both exist as finite numbers but LHL ≠ RHL; the two-sided limit therefore does not exist.
**Worked example.** For f(x) = |x|/x at 0, LHL = −1 and RHL = 1, so the graph has a step of height 2 at the origin.
**Step functions.** The greatest-integer function [x] jumps by 1 at every integer n, since lim(x→n⁻) [x] = n − 1 and lim(x→n⁺) [x] = n.
**Piecewise rules.** A jump usually appears at the boundary between two branches; evaluate each branch at a and compare the two results.
**Not removable.** Because the mismatch comes from the behaviour on both sides of a, changing only f(a) cannot make the function continuous.
**Exam caution.** Report both one-sided limits with their values; saying only 'limit does not exist' loses the marks for identifying the jump size.
summary: A jump occurs when both one-sided limits exist and are finite but unequal; no redefinition of the single value f(a) can remove it.
